titleStmt.title: Paper Prepared in the Department of Defense

div.head: Paper Prepared in the Department of Defense

list.label: a.
list.item: What will be the effect of the appraisal of the relative merits of alternative target systems, directed by NSC Action No. 2009, upon the size and composition of the striking force?
list.label: b.
list.item: In the light of the appraisal referred to in a above, what is the most desirable mix of missile systems from the point of view of our optimum strategic nuclear striking capacity on the one hand, and from the point of view of the greatest degree of invulnerability on the other hand, and can these be easily reconciled?
list.label: c.
list.item: Is there a valid requirement to develop another generation of strategic bombers, taking into account the probable capabilities of enemy defenses and the problems of maintaining such aircraft in an alert status?
list.label: d.
list.item: Would it be desirable to extend the effectiveness of POLARIS missiles by adapting them for use on surface vessels, and on land bases, assuming the development of an appropriate mobile launching unit?
list.label: e.
list.item: Should further priority be given to MINUTE MAN by the earlier establishment of a production capability and by seeking to afford it more mobility? What effect would further emphasis on MINUTE MAN have on the TITAN and ATLAS missiles program?
list.label: f.
list.item: What is the proper balance between procurement of additional retaliatory weapons and expenditures to protect those now available against surprise attack?

list.label: a.
list.item: What are the best means for defending the striking force? What mixture of active defenses, hardening, dispersal, and quick reaction leads to the greatest certainty of survival for the striking force? How does this best mix change with Soviet capabilities?
list.label: b.
list.item: Assuming that point defenses will be required, what areas are to be protected—SAC bases or urban industrial areas, or both?
list.label: c.
list.item: In the light of the changing nature of the Soviet attack capability, how should air defenses be allocated as between the manned bomber threat and the ballistic missile threat?
list.label: d.
list.item:
Are our present programs for early warning against aircraft and missiles adequate to the changing threat? Will our communications
have the certainty and reliability to insure that all forces can respond when warning is received?
list.label: e.
list.item: What facilities have we now for determining that our bases are under attack? What facilities for disseminating this information?
list.label: f.
list.item: Will the concept of perimeter, area and point defense continue to have validity in the 1960–65 period?
list.label: g.
list.item: What is an appropriate balance between manned interceptors, interceptor missiles and ground-to-air missiles?
list.label: h.
list.item: To what extent do our present continental defenses meet the threat of missiles launched from submarines? What measures have promise to be effective against this threat?
list.label: i.
list.item: Is there a need for more centralized management of the various aspects of continental air defense?

list.label: a.
list.item: In what ways can our present ASW capability be improved?
list.label: b.
list.item: Should further emphasis be placed on methods for broad ocean surveillance?
list.label: c.
list.item:
Is the effort currently being devoted to ASW commensurate with the threat: (1)
against the continental U.S.? (2)
against task forces and against shipping?
list.label: d.
list.item: Is there a need for more effective, centralized direction of the ASW effort?

list.label: a.
list.item: In the event of general war involving a nuclear exchange, is it assumed that there will be a requirement for further deployment of ground forces overseas? If so, can the probable requirements be determined?
list.label: b.
list.item: Taking into account our commitments and the nature of the threat with respect to hostilities short of general war, do our tactical forces have adequate mobility, flexibility and readiness? Should this requirement have priority over mobilization reserves for general war?
list.label: c.
list.item: Do present programs provide aircraft and weapons wholly appropriate to such tactical combat?
list.label: d.
list.item: Is there a need for so many different tactical weapons (i.e., the 280-mm gun, the 8-inch howitzer, the 155-mm howitzer, HONEST JOHN, LITTLE JOHN, LACROSSE, SERGEANT)?
list.label: e.
list.item: Is there an element of overlap between the Army’s growing arsenal of short-range missiles and the Air Force’s tactical aircraft; and if so, is this desirable?
list.label: f.
list.item: What will be the requirement for small nuclear weapons to equip ground forces? Can this requirement be met by our programmed production capabilities?
list.label: g.
list.item: Is there an appropriate balance between the amount of resources being devoted to BW–CW procurement and those devoted to research?
